targets.name: Wellington to General Maitland
targets.next: HathiTrust closed 03:37 UTC: 19 more editions tested through the Bibliographic and Extracted Features APIs, none matches (76 editions in all); Scott, Jones 1800, London Perry, Walker 1810 and Dublin Entick are not in HathiTrust at all. Full report in DICTIONARY.md. Tomokiyo, Hayes and Lasry are also on this item. wait.unblock: Spink confirms or denies a dictionary in the lot; or a library check of Urban and the Bentinck papers.

targets.name: Charles Whitworth to Robert Harley
targets.ref: TNA SP 91/5/108 (+ ff. 106, 121 for the key)
targets.next: Decide whether one unread clause is worth about 10 images (roughly £30). If yes, order SP 91/5/108, 106 and 121 on Discovery using the message in ciphers/whitworth-1707/REQUEST.md.
targets.note: Worker result 19 Sept 2026: four of the five 'undeciphered' items are already in print (Sbornik vols 39 and 50) or deciphered in the same volume. Only one clause of f. 108 is unread, about the French mediation of 1707. The neighbours ff. 106 and 121 were deciphered in London, so their pages give the key. Low historical weight; cheap; certain to work. Blind sweep 20 Sept 2026: no prior attempt found; open, narrowed to one clause of f.108.

wait.on: Your decision and your click on the TNA order
wait.expected: Whenever you choose; TNA then takes 2 to 4 weeks
wait.unblock: Order placed. If you decide it is not worth it, mark it parked and it drops down the queue.

targets.result: Four of five "undeciphered" items were already in print; the finding corrects the catalogue.

targets.name: Eckert Papers, US Military Telegraph
targets.ref: Huntington mssEC 15 (1862); mssEC 19 ledger with cipher book mssEC 41 (1864)
targets.next: Parked for cryptanalysis (every cipher in the ledger reads from a surviving book). An enquiry went to the Huntington curator on 20 Sept 2026 asking whether a corpus-level decoding dataset exists and whether one would be useful; their reply decides whether the mechanical corpus pass is run as an edition project.
targets.note: Twenty 1864 entries read at grade H from cipher book mssEC 41; seventeen agree word for word with the Official Records, one with the printed Lincoln works, two (E4, E5) not found in the sources listed in AUDIT.md. Corpus question (AUDIT.md section 12): no one has mapped the ledger entries to cipher, key, plaintext and print; the project's decoding phase was never launched (paused Jan 2018, ended July 2019). A mechanical corpus pass over the volunteer transcriptions is possible and cheap, but it is an edition, not a solve.

wait.on: The Huntington (curator reply to the 20 Sept enquiry)
wait.unblock: A reply saying no such dataset exists and it would be useful; then a capped corpus pass over the volunteer transcriptions with decode.py and decode_no2.py.

targets.result: Machine-readable Cipher No. 1 and No. 2 keys, 23 readings checked against print, an audit with N-classes, and a corpus-status finding, offered to the Huntington on 20 Sept 2026.

targets.next: Verified 20 Sept 2026: BL catalogue confirms the item; no solution found by the sweep; English plaintext near-certain. For you: ask BL Imaging Services for a quote for f.423 (REQUEST.md); a Reader Pass may be required, so ask whether they will quote remotely.
targets.note: Key leads: Monck's correspondence with Clarges and Hyde in the Clarendon State Papers and Thurloe. HMC 5th and 7th Reports describe the collection and can be checked in print first.

wait.unblock: A quote and a scan of f.423.

targets.name: Unidentified 18th-century cipher manuscript
targets.ref: National Library of Scotland MS.20769: "Unidentified text, apparently 18th century, written in cipher"; 57 leaves, oblong quarto and octavo; genre "Ciphers. Codes."
targets.next: Catalogue record read first-hand 04:32 UTC (Wayback capture of the NLS page; the live site still throws a Cloudflare challenge even with the browser fix). Confirmed: 57 leaves, cipher alphabet of Roman and Greek letters, astrological and invented symbols, text divided into sections, a name "Baptiste Romin or Romain" pencilled on ff. 27-28, deposited 1949 by the Society of Antiquaries of Scotland, language undetermined. For you: decide on scans. At GBP 1.80 per A4 scan, 57 leaves both sides is roughly GBP 100-200; REQUEST.md suggests asking NLS for a quote and for a sample of a few leaves first.
targets.note: Size is the point: 57 leaves of a genuine cipher is far above unicity for a homophonic system. Risk, still open: the cataloguer's genre tag is not proof it is a cipher rather than a private notation. A sample of five leaves would settle that before the full order.

wait.on: You: ask NLS for a quote and a five-leaf sample (REQUEST.md)
wait.expected: NLS reprographics answer in one to two weeks
wait.unblock: Sample images; a worker classifies the symbol system and decides whether to order the rest.
